name: System
description: Intent architecture for a VS Code agent that embodies its interaction state through a local Blender-driven avatar.

attributes.name: GRAPH_USAGE_GUIDE
attributes.description: 将本文件作为意图架构知识图谱与行动约束入口使用，而不是静态清单。阅读和行动时遵循以下规则：1. 优先把本图谱当作当前任务的第一事实来源，先通读相关元素、relationships、views、attributes、testcases，再决定是否继续读取代码、测试、脚本、文档或其它外部文件。2. 本图谱以Archimate建模语言为主，辅之其它建模语言（如UML等）；所有Archimate元素的语义都以Archimate标准定义为准，不得仅凭元素名称或自然语言习惯随意改写。3. 凡属性、description、browser_path、acceptanceCriteria或其它字段指向仓库路径、#file、#sym 或外部模型线索时，应将其视为需要按需追溯的证据入口；引用内容用于补充上下文，不得推翻图谱中已经明确写出的原则、约束、显性testcase与关系语义。4. 该图谱中若存在 `Archimate_principle`、`Archimate_constrain` 等元素，你必须优先识别并严格服从；它们是硬约束，用来限制你的推理、设计与行动边界，你不能超过这些约束。5. 遇到信息冲突时，按以下优先级处理：硬约束元素与原则 > 显性testcase及意图架构显式语义 > 元素、关系、视图、attributes中的明确描述 > 被引用文件或符号 > 当前代码现状；代码只是实现证据，不会自动覆盖意图。6. 显性testcase是意图架构验收基线。除非任务明确属于意图架构设计并要求更新基线，否则你不得擅自新增、删除、重建或改写显性testcase的目标、挂载对象、断言口径与范围；编码或修复阶段只能补齐其可执行入口、支撑性实现、支撑性测试与运行环境。7. 修改边界必须清晰：意图架构设计阶段负责更新意图元素、关系、视图与显性testcase；实现架构设计阶段负责维护实现架构；编码阶段默认修改代码、测试、脚本和文档，不得把实现偏差直接回写成意图漂移。8. 分析问题时必须沿追溯链理解上下文，不得只看单个元素名称或单段description；至少应综合相关元素、关系、视图、上下游依赖、引用文件与测试挂载点后再下结论。9. 当图谱信息不完整时，可以基于仓库证据做最小必要推断，但必须显式标记假设，且不得臆造不存在的外部接口、SLA、部署事实、组织流程或新的显性验收基线。10. 若需要新增支撑性测试、实现护栏或运行环境说明，应优先写入实现架构、代码、测试与对应文档的正确落点，而不是污染意图层。11. 最终输出必须能说明：你读取了哪些图谱证据，遵守了哪些原则或约束，哪些结论是仓库已证实事实，哪些内容只是带标记的最小假设。

elements.name: EmbodiedAgentInteraction
elements.description: The product capability that lets the VS Code agent express its live interaction state and bounded user-requested semantic avatar feedback through a local anthropomorphic avatar.

attributes.name: acceptance_outcomes
attributes.content:
The capability is limited to local-machine-first operation for the first baseline.
Avatar behavior is presentation-layer feedback and must not replace the assistant's core task behavior.
The first baseline covers facial expression plus a small set of simple body gestures.
Bounded user-requested semantic avatar actions are allowed in addition to the default lifecycle-driven embodiment flow.

testcases.name: TC-EX-001 ResponseStartEmbodiment
testcases.description: When the assistant begins a qualifying response, the avatar should enter a bounded thinking or acknowledging state through the mediator. Control point: the agent enters a qualifying response-start lifecycle state and the mediator selects a semantic avatar action. Observation point: Blender returns structured acknowledgement and resulting face or gesture state transition for the targeted avatar channel.
testcases.Input: Control point: AgentResponseLifecycleState drives AvatarEmbodimentMediator during response-start. Involved elements: EmbodiedAgentInteraction, ApprovedAvatarActionVocabulary, TruthfulEmbodimentPrinciple, AvatarEmbodimentMediator, AgentResponseLifecycleState, LocalBlenderAvatarEndpoint, StructuredAvatarExecutionFeedback.
testcases.TestResults: Observation point: structured Blender feedback confirms a thinking-compatible or acknowledging-compatible state transition. The selected action comes from the approved semantic vocabulary. The action begins within a sub-second target envelope under normal local conditions. The observed state is compatible with truthful thinking or acknowledging semantics. Explicit acceptance baseline owned by EmbodiedAgentInteraction. Baseline evidence: #file:tests/explicit/response-start-embodiment.test.ts. Executable entrypoint: #file:scripts/run-tc-ex-001.mjs

testcases.name: TC-EX-002 ResponseCompleteEmbodiment
testcases.description: When the assistant completes a qualifying response, the avatar should transition into a bounded confirming or settling state. Control point: the agent enters a qualifying response-complete lifecycle state and the mediator selects a semantic confirming or settling action. Observation point: Blender returns structured acknowledgement and resulting face or gesture state transition for the targeted avatar channel.
testcases.Input: Control point: AgentResponseLifecycleState drives AvatarEmbodimentMediator during response-complete. Involved elements: EmbodiedAgentInteraction, ApprovedAvatarActionVocabulary, TruthfulEmbodimentPrinciple, InteractionStateDrivenEmbodiment, AvatarEmbodimentMediator, AgentResponseLifecycleState, LocalBlenderAvatarEndpoint, StructuredAvatarExecutionFeedback.
testcases.TestResults: Observation point: structured Blender feedback confirms a confirming-compatible or settling-compatible state transition. The selected action remains within the approved semantic vocabulary. The observed state is compatible with truthful completion or confirmation semantics. If a stale prior action exists, the newer completion state takes priority. Explicit acceptance baseline owned by EmbodiedAgentInteraction. Baseline evidence: #file:tests/explicit/response-complete-embodiment.test.ts. Executable entrypoint: #file:scripts/run-tc-ex-002.mjs

testcases.name: TC-EX-003 BlenderDisconnectGracefulDegradation
testcases.description: If Blender is unavailable, disconnected, or rejects a command, the assistant keeps functioning while avatar embodiment degrades safely. Control point: the mediator attempts a semantic avatar action against the local Blender endpoint while the endpoint is unavailable or rejecting commands. Observation point: structured feedback or surfaced status indicates avatar degradation, while the assistant response continues and recovery semantics return toward neutral idle.
testcases.Input: Control point: AvatarEmbodimentMediator executes a semantic avatar action against LocalBlenderAvatarEndpoint during a disconnect or rejection condition. Involved elements: EmbodiedAgentInteraction, TruthfulEmbodimentPrinciple, GracefulAvatarDegradationConstraint, AvatarEmbodimentMediator, LocalBlenderAvatarEndpoint, StructuredAvatarExecutionFeedback.
testcases.TestResults: Observation point: surfaced degradation status and recovery semantics return toward neutral idle while the assistant's core response loop continues. Avatar degradation is surfaced explicitly rather than silently ignored. The recovery target is neutral idle semantics rather than an arbitrary lingering pose. Explicit acceptance baseline owned by EmbodiedAgentInteraction. Baseline evidence: #file:tests/explicit/blender-disconnect-graceful-degradation.test.ts. Executable entrypoint: #file:scripts/run-tc-ex-003.mjs

testcases.name: TC-EX-004 UserSemanticAvatarRequestEmbodiment
testcases.description: When the user submits a bounded natural-language semantic avatar request, the system should translate that request into an approved avatar action and execute it through the mediator. Control point: the user submits the canonical request 'show a thinking state' through UserSemanticAvatarControlInterface, which becomes a UserSemanticAvatarActionRequest that triggers the mediator. Observation point: Blender returns structured acknowledgement and a resulting thinking-compatible state transition for the targeted avatar channel.
testcases.Input: Control point: UserSemanticAvatarControlInterface submits the canonical request 'show a thinking state', producing UserSemanticAvatarActionRequest for AvatarEmbodimentMediator. Involved elements: EmbodiedAgentInteraction, ApprovedAvatarActionVocabulary, TruthfulEmbodimentPrinciple, UserDirectedSemanticEmbodiment, UserSemanticAvatarControlInterface, UserSemanticAvatarActionRequest, AvatarEmbodimentMediator, LocalBlenderAvatarEndpoint, StructuredAvatarExecutionFeedback.
testcases.TestResults: Observation point: structured Blender feedback confirms a thinking-compatible state transition and acknowledges delivery for the canonical semantic request. The selected action remains inside the approved semantic vocabulary and does not expose raw rig, bone, shape key, or scene manipulation semantics. Explicit acceptance baseline owned by EmbodiedAgentInteraction. Baseline evidence: #file:tests/explicit/user-semantic-avatar-request-embodiment.test.ts. Executable entrypoint: #file:scripts/run-tc-ex-004.mjs

elements.name: ApprovedAvatarActionVocabulary
elements.description: A closed first-phase semantic action set bounded to neutral, thinking, acknowledging, confirming, restrained apology, and a few simple gestures.

attributes.name: acceptance_outcomes
attributes.content:
Intent exposes only semantic avatar actions such as expression and gesture primitives.
Intent does not baseline raw rig, bone, shape key, or scene manipulation.
Threatening, sexualized, deceptive, or highly exaggerated affect is forbidden.
The same bounded vocabulary applies to both lifecycle-driven embodiment and user-requested semantic avatar control.

elements.name: TruthfulEmbodimentPrinciple
elements.description: Avatar affect may vary stylistically, but its semantics must stay aligned with actual assistant state, including uncertainty and failure.

attributes.name: acceptance_outcomes
attributes.content:
The avatar must not display confidence that exceeds the assistant's actual certainty.
Uncertainty must be expressed with an uncertainty-compatible state.
Failure embodiment is restrained neutral or apology rather than dramatic distress.

elements.name: GracefulAvatarDegradationConstraint
elements.description: Avatar channel failure must degrade safely without aborting the assistant's primary interaction loop.

attributes.name: acceptance_outcomes
attributes.content:
If Blender is unavailable or rejects a command, the assistant continues its core response.
Avatar status is surfaced as degraded or unavailable.
Recovery returns the avatar semantics to neutral idle by default.

elements.name: UserAvatarOverrideConstraint
elements.description: Users must be able to disable avatar behavior independently from the assistant's reasoning and task execution.

attributes.name: acceptance_outcomes
attributes.content:
Mute or disable suppresses Blender avatar actions only.
The assistant's task behavior and status reporting continue normally.
Manual puppeteering and raw rig manipulation are out of the first baseline.
Bounded user semantic avatar requests remain allowed through the approved semantic control interface.

elements.name: InteractionStateDrivenEmbodiment
elements.description: The default embodied experience is driven by the agent's own interaction lifecycle instead of manual scene direction.

attributes.name: acceptance_outcomes
attributes.content:
The first baseline reacts to response-start and response-complete lifecycle states by default.
The newest relevant interaction state takes priority over stale animation unless a user-requested semantic action is explicitly issued for the current action turn.
Lip sync, voice, camera, lighting, and scene control are out of scope for the first baseline.

elements.name: AvatarEmbodimentMediator
elements.description: A mediation layer inside the VS Code agent that maps actual agent state to bounded avatar actions.

attributes.name: acceptance_outcomes
attributes.content:
The mediator selects actions from the approved semantic vocabulary only.
The mediator may trigger actions automatically during the agent response lifecycle and may also execute bounded user-requested semantic actions.
A user-requested semantic action may take single-action priority over the default lifecycle-driven action for the current control turn.
The mediator remains separate from raw Blender rig internals at intent level.

elements.name: AgentResponseLifecycleState
elements.description: The qualifying internal state transitions that drive first-phase avatar embodiment, including response-start, uncertainty, completion, and degraded conditions.

elements.name: AvatarMuteOverride
elements.description: The user-visible control that suppresses avatar actions without suppressing the assistant itself.

elements.name: UserDirectedSemanticEmbodiment
elements.description: A bounded user-directed embodiment flow that lets the user request approved semantic avatar actions without exposing low-level Blender control.

attributes.name: acceptance_outcomes
attributes.content:
The user can request only approved semantic avatar actions.
A user-requested semantic action applies to the current requested control turn rather than permanently replacing lifecycle-driven embodiment.
Raw rig, bone, shape key, and general scene automation remain out of scope.

elements.name: UserSemanticAvatarControlInterface
elements.description: The user-visible semantic control interface that accepts natural-language avatar requests and submits them as bounded semantic actions.

attributes.name: acceptance_outcomes
attributes.content:
The interface accepts natural-language semantic requests rather than low-level Blender commands.
The interface must keep requests within the approved semantic vocabulary.
The interface does not baseline a specific host channel such as a single custom-agent implementation.

elements.name: UserSemanticAvatarActionRequest
elements.description: The bounded semantic avatar action request produced from a user natural-language request after it has been reduced to the approved semantic vocabulary.

attributes.name: acceptance_outcomes
attributes.content:
The event carries only approved semantic action intent.
The event excludes raw rig, bone, shape key, and scene manipulation payloads.
The canonical first-baseline request 'show a thinking state' must resolve to a thinking-compatible action.

elements.name: LocalBlenderAvatarEndpoint
elements.description: The first-phase local Blender execution endpoint for one specific avatar rig on the same machine as the VS Code agent.

attributes.name: acceptance_outcomes
attributes.content:
The first baseline assumes local-machine-only integration.
Only avatar face and simple body gesture channels are in scope.
The endpoint is not a general Blender scene automation baseline.

elements.name: StructuredAvatarExecutionFeedback
elements.description: Structured Blender feedback that acknowledges an avatar action and exposes resulting state or transition information for validation.

attributes.name: acceptance_outcomes
attributes.content:
Intent acceptance does not rely on human visual inspection alone.
Each qualifying action yields observable delivery and effect semantics.
Feedback is sufficient to support explicit testcase observation points.

relationships.description: The local Blender avatar endpoint yields structured execution and state feedback.

relationships.name: observes_feedback

relationships.statement: AvatarMuteOverride associates with AvatarEmbodimentMediator to suppress avatar actions.
relationships.name: suppresses_avatar_actions

relationships.name: bounds_user_semantic_control
